name: MAW
description: Maw is a historic trick-taking card game that was popular in 16th century Britain and Ireland. It is the ancestor of the Irish game Spoil Five and other related games. Played with a distinctive 52-card deck where the 5 and 9 of trumps have special powers, Maw features unique ranking orders and the ability to renege (not follow suit) under specific circumstances.

content.text: Maw is a historic trick-taking card game that was popular in 16th century Britain and Ireland. It is the ancestor of the Irish game Spoil Five and other related games. Played with a distinctive 52-card deck where the 5 and 9 of trumps have special powers, Maw features unique ranking orders and the ability to renege (not follow suit) under specific circumstances.

Maw was extremely popular in 16th century Britain, played at the court of James I. It spread to Ireland where it evolved into Spoil Five and related games like Twenty-Five, Forty-Five, and One Hundred and Ten.
2-10 players (best with 5-7). Can be played individually or in partnerships.
Standard 52-card deck. In trump suits, cards rank: 5 (highest), J, A, K, Q, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 4, 3, 2. In non-trump suits: K (high), Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, A (low).
Standard deck, chips or counters for scoring.
5 cards to each player, dealt in packets. Remaining cards form the stock.

items.text: Spoil Five: The Irish descendant of Maw with more complex scoring and the 'spoiling' mechanic.
Twenty-Five: Modern Irish game descended from Maw, played to 25 points.
Forty-Five: Popular in Atlantic Canada, descended from Maw traditions.
